thread:
Mia S: Heads up — NovaHealth perf run scheduled tomorrow 10am PT. Need final check on load plan, model shard, KV cache warmup, and cost calc. They're planning 200 qps sustained with ~2k token responses. @Alex R can you confirm GPU choice? @Jordan P can you prep the k6 target and metrics?

Alex R: Recommend pinning to dedicated a100-80gb pool (dedicated-2). 200 qps with 2k tokens ~= 400k tokens/s so we need batching + warmed KV cache. We'll run fp16 + q4f16 quant profile. Latency SLO request = p95 < 200ms — we can aim for that but expect spikes if cache cold.

Jordan P: Pushed a k6 script to the perf repo (see /perf/novahealth/scripts). Ramp plan: 1m ramp to 200 qps, 30m steady, 5m cool-down. Collect p50/p95/p99, tail, tokens/sec, error rate. Model: xlarge-v1-ffn. Run cmd sample: ```k6 run --vus 200 --duration 36m script.js```

Mia S: Also customer asked about a short burst to 500 qps for 2 minutes during demo. Ops question: can we support 500 qps for 2m w/o coldstart errors?

Alex R: Yes if we configure burst headroom. Recommend baseline: 4 replicas (steady) with autoscale + 1-2 GPU burst nodes. Important: run KV cache pre-warm for 10 minutes. If miss rate high during initial minutes, tail latency jumps.

Jordan P: I'll add pre-warm step to the run: ```for i in $(seq 1 10000); do curl -XPOST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d @warm_payload.json; done``` — doing that for 10m before ramp.

Tess (benchbot): Scheduled loadtest job 4823456789 started by Jordan P. Notifying #eng-runtime.

Jordan P: Post-run quick metrics: p50 110ms, p95 260ms, p99 480ms, errors 0.4% (mainly timeouts at peak burst). GPU avg utilization (a100-80gb) ~78% during steady. Token throughput ~360k/sec (below worst-case estimate because batching kicked in). Observed KV miss rate ~18% for first 6 minutes, then dropped to ~2% after warm.

Alex R: Actionable notes: KV miss explains the p95/p99 spikes. Recommend enabling prefix caching + warm-up in production, or reserve ~10% extra capacity for bursts. Cost estimate for the test (incl pre-warm + burst headroom): ~$1.8k for the 1h window — I'll send a line-item spreadsheet.

Mia S: Customer requested an official run writeup including failure modes and mitigation recommendations. Jordan — can you draft the runbook + one-page results summary for NovaHealth by EOD so I can attach to the SOW?

Jordan P: On it. Draft uploaded to the Google Drive (drive.redwood/novaperf/summary.pdf) — will paste bullets here when ready.

NovaHealth (customer): Thanks team — promising. Quick Q: does using HSM/KMS for key ops add notable latency? Also we need an enterprise security questionnaire (KMS, audit logs, data residency).

Alex R: HSM/KMS adds negligible latency at the token-generation path (order of single-digit ms) if keys are cached and requests don't call remote KMS per token. We'll include a short KMS latency test and answer the security questionnaire.

Mia S: :thumbsup: Great. Tagging @ops for final SLA language and @legal for SOW wording. I'll send the final report to NovaHealth after Jordan's draft and Alex's cost sheet are in.

Jordan P: Final note — we saw one transient 503 from a sidecar during peak; added a retry (exponential backoff) to the client as a mitigation. Will document in runbook.
